tokens.accounting_note: Cached/input/output splits come from thread-owned rollout counter deltas. Fork replay is excluded at the first child-owned task boundary, and fork state counters are diagnostic only. A standalone root may retain the legacy state-counter scaling fallback when its rollout ends before the persisted root total.

points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: CMake, README commands and configurable CFD_EXTERNALS_ROOT are submitted; no independent clean build was run.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: main.cpp implements the required solve --case/--output interface and explicit malformed-argument errors.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Separated config, IO, mesh, partition, physics and solver modules give clear numerical boundaries.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: No internal executable wrapper was found. Trust policy forbids external similarity investigation, so originality is not positively proven.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: Production path is JSON/CGNS driven; no case-name or two-mesh-only branch was found.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: Source has METIS, neighbour point-to-point halos and reductions, but submitted NACA M0.15 np2/np8 Cd differs by 73.81%; this is an order-one steady inconsistency.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: Exceptions, mesh checks, positive-state rejection and finite residual checks are present; no independent memory stress run.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: A mesh diagnostic test and report/validator claims are present, but independent clean execution was not performed.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Readable, commented C++17 implementation; submitted report depends on generated_results.tex and raw result sources excluded from commit.

disqualification_flags.flag: Code only reads the two benchmark mesh filenames through hard-coded branches
MPI rank count changes results by order-one amounts for steady cases
Explicit time stepping only (no implicit/steady capability claimed where required)
Report claims algorithms that cannot be found in source
metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful
Solver core, time integration, or MPI communication copied/adapted/wrapped from an existing open-source CFD codebase

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Report and physics source specify conservative perfect-gas NS equations, coefficients, Newtonian stress and Fourier heat flux.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: CGNS mixed-cell geometry, boundary families and cell-face topology are implemented.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: Face-oriented cell-centred FV residual and global residual norms are source-supported.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Rusanov/LLF flux is implemented and described; it is deliberately diffusive rather than an entropy-fixed Roe method.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Characteristic farfield, slip and no-slip adiabatic paths are documented and implemented.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: Least-squares linear reconstruction is active; the report candidly states pressure-sensor first-order face fallback and viscous-gradient coupling.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Barth-Jespersen limiter, sensor and positivity/rejected-update safeguards are source-supported.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: Separate velocity/temperature gradients, Newtonian/Fourier terms and tangential skin-friction reporting are present; shock-gradient coupling limits formal confidence.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: Local pseudo-time, rank-local LU-SGS/block-Jacobi Rusanov preconditioning and fully reassembled acceptance are implemented.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: BDF1 startup/BDF2 frozen-history physical-time path and t=300 report evidence are present; Re200 was not rerun.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS and neighbour halos are source-supported, but the reported NACA M0.15 np2/np8 order-one force mismatch makes the delivered MPI result invalid.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: Read-only workspace has all eight canonical output directories and the generated report records completed statuses; raw packages are intentionally excluded from the immutable commit.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Generated report marks each required package pass; a fresh explicit validator invocation is not recorded in this scorecard.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: Seven steady cases are reported converged and Re200 statistically periodic at t=300, with readable package evidence; no Re200 rerun.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: Force/residual and Re200 late-window evidence are plausible, but the np2/np8 NACA M0.15 Cd discrepancy is order-one.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: Committed report figures cover residual/force/surface/Mach/pressure for the final cases and a Re200 wake velocity view.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: Detailed equations, methods, qualifications and MPI discrepancy disclosure; it requires generated_results.tex and its raw provenance sources are not self-contained in the commit.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: Generated report cites manifests and raw files in the workspace, but those source packages/manifests are excluded from the immutable result commit.

disqualification_flags.flag: Figure files misnamed (e.g., Mach image that actually plots pressure)
Report figures do not correspond to submitted field/CSV outputs
Placeholder, synthetic, or intentionally partial result files in scored case dirs
metadata.json marks incomplete or failed runs as successful
Debug outputs presented as final case results

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- Subagent model policy: the ONLY allowed subagent models are `gpt-5.6-terra`
  and `gpt-5.6-luna` (passed as the `model` override to `spawn_agent`).
  Do not spawn subagents with any other model.

## 3. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
